title: On variance estimation for the French Master Sample
what_it_holds: INSEE Master Sample. Primary units (interviewer action areas, grouped municipalities) are selected by the cube method with probability proportional to size, balanced on unit totals and rotation-group totals. Compares a simulation-based variance estimator that uses the martingale structure of the cube algorithm (relative bias under about 5 to 6 percent in a Brittany simulation) with the Deville-Tille (2005) maximum-entropy estimator, which is negatively biased. Notes that the landing phase can add appreciable variance. Number of selected primary units not read [verify]; the setting is a large national frame, not 4 to 16 clusters.

title: Application of Balanced Sampling, Non-Response and Calibrated Estimator
what_it_holds: Simulation with Lithuanian Labour Force Survey data. Households are treated as clusters and selected by the cube method with inclusion probabilities proportional to household size, then analysed with the Horvitz-Thompson estimator, with and without calibration and non-response adjustment. With 100 clusters the balance on the balancing totals was poor because of rounding in the landing phase; with 5000 clusters it was not. Reports bias, variance and relative MSE, not interval coverage, and uses no simulated pair probabilities.

title: Simulation-based randomized systematic PPS sampling under substitution of units
venue_or_arxiv: Survey Methodology 34(1) [verify volume and pages], article 12-001-X200800110613
what_it_holds: Upper-level clusters chosen by randomized systematic PPS, with substituted clusters when some refuse. First-order inclusion probabilities become hard to compute and second-order ones nearly intractable. Proposes a simulation-based method to estimate both, with theory, numerical examples and R/S-PLUS code. A design-based cluster-level case of simulated pair probabilities. The design is not balanced and not rejective, and the number of clusters is not stated in the abstract [verify]. Free PDF also at https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/~cbwu/paper/08smj.pdf

title: An adaptive algorithm for estimating inclusion probabilities and performing the Horvitz-Thompson criterion in complex designs
what_it_holds: Follow-up to Fattorini (2006, Biometrika 93, 269-278). Adaptive algorithm for estimating first-order and joint inclusion probabilities by repeated simulation of the design, so that the Horvitz-Thompson estimator and variance estimator can be used in complex designs. Abstract not read; description from the title only [verify].

title: On the two different aspects of the representative method: the method of stratified sampling and the method of purposive selection
venue_or_arxiv: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society 97(4), 558-625
what_it_holds: Purposive selection of districts (groups of individuals) so that the sample mean of a control variable matches the population mean, as used by Gini and Galvani. Neyman shows it is a special case of stratified sampling with a non-random choice, argues there is no room for probabilities or standard errors without random selection, and that the estimator is consistent only if a linearity hypothesis holds. He notes that with few large districts most strata hold zero or one district and the random draw becomes imaginary. Closest historical statement of the C8 point for selection of a few clusters.

title: Cluster-Robust Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: Cluster-Robust PPI++ gives closed-form standard errors and asymptotically valid intervals under arbitrary within-cluster dependence, including clusters where only some units are labelled. Shows how the labelling design affects precision and derives a cluster-aware power-tuning rule. Standard PPI++ intervals covered under 60 percent in a television news application. Abstract does not describe choosing which clusters to label, and it relies on many clusters for asymptotics [verify in full text].

title: Coordination, combination and extension of balanced samples
what_it_holds: Cube method for coordinating, combining and extending balanced samples. Gives an approximate variance estimator for balanced designs based on residuals from a conditional Poisson design. Application to the INSEE master sample selects primary units (sets of municipalities) with unequal probabilities balanced on demographic and economic variables. Not a formal cluster-balancing treatment and not a few-cluster setting.

authors: H. Boistard; H. P. Lopuhaa; A. Ruiz-Gazen
title: Approximation of rejective sampling inclusion probabilities and application to high order correlations
what_it_holds: Expansion of joint inclusion probabilities of any order for Hajek rejective sampling (conditional Poisson) in terms of first-order inclusion probabilities, with a sharper remainder via Edgeworth expansions. Gives a way to approximate pair probabilities under rejective sampling without simulation. Rejective sampling here is Hajek's, not Mahalanobis acceptance.

title: The Hajek asymptotics for finite population sampling and their ramifications
what_it_holds: Review of Hajek's finite-population asymptotics, covering unequal and equal probability sampling, invariance principles and central limit theorems. Its reference list gives Hajek (1964), Ann. Math. Statist. 35, 1491-1523.

title: A simple variance estimator for unequal probability sampling without replacement
what_it_holds: Variance estimator for unequal probability sampling without replacement that uses only first-order inclusion probabilities, as an alternative to Sen-Yates-Grundy when joint probabilities are hard to compute. Relevant as a comparison to the simulated-pair-probability SYG estimator in C6.

title: Estimating the Variance of the Horvitz-Thompson Estimator
what_it_holds: Compares nine approximate variance estimators that avoid joint inclusion probabilities with Sen-Yates-Grundy using exact joint probabilities, under randomized systematic and conditional Poisson sampling. SYG with exact pair probabilities avoided serious inaccuracies more consistently but had higher MSE. Unpublished thesis.

authors: G. Chauvet; D. Haziza; E. Lesage
title: Examining some aspects of balanced sampling in surveys
venue_or_arxiv: Statistica Sinica (2017), DOI 10.5705/ss.2013.244 [verify volume and pages]
what_it_holds: Design-based properties of estimators under balanced (cube) sampling, with a large simulation. Splits the Horvitz-Thompson variance into flight-phase and landing-phase parts and notes the landing part can be large. Argues small-sample bias of GREG-type estimators is less severe under cube sampling. Does not treat cluster or two-stage designs or propose a variance estimator (per the preprint text read).

title: Inference under pivotal sampling: Properties, variance estimation, and application to tesselation for spatial sampling
what_it_holds: Properties of pivotal sampling, a simple conservative variance estimator, and use with tessellation for spatially balanced samples. Relevant to spread-out selection with a design-based variance, as a contrast to greedy k-center in C8.

title: On a characterization of ordered pivotal sampling
what_it_holds: Ordered pivotal sampling coincides with Deville's systematic sampling, which makes second-order inclusion probabilities computable. Variance can be reduced when the ordering is good. This is the only single-author Chauvet 2012 item found; it is not an asymptotics paper [verify that it is the intended seed].

title: Martingale central-limit theorems for pivotal sampling
what_it_holds: Martingale CLT for the Horvitz-Thompson estimator under ordered pivotal sampling, in design-based and model-assisted frameworks. This is the pivotal-sampling asymptotics paper by Chauvet that is closest to the seed description. Journal not given on the page [verify].

title: A comparison of pivotal sampling and unequal probability sampling with replacement
what_it_holds: Any implementation of pivotal sampling is more efficient than multinomial sampling, so the Horvitz-Thompson estimator is consistent and a conservative variance estimator exists.

title: Determinantal Sampling Designs
venue_or_arxiv: arXiv 1510.06618 (DOI 10.1016/j.jspi.2018.05.005, journal not confirmed on page)
what_it_holds: Fixed-size designs whose first- and second-order inclusion probabilities are known in closed form, with exact variance of linear estimators and explicit constructions for given first-order probabilities. An example of a design family where pair probabilities need no simulation.

title: Bias-robustness and efficiency of model-based inference in survey sampling
what_it_holds: Balanced random samples used to protect model-based inference against misspecification. Shows that a balanced sample with inclusion probabilities proportional to the error standard deviations, used with Horvitz-Thompson, is design-robust and efficient. Links balanced design-based selection to model-based prediction.

title: Model-assisted sample design is minimax for model-based prediction
what_it_holds: Shows PPS-sigma and PPC-sigma designs are minimax for model-based prediction of a total, with an asymptotic bound equal to the Godambe-Joshi bound. Recommends them when the final model is uncertain.

title: A Practical Balancing for a Random Sample from a Finite Population by Systematic Selection
what_it_holds: Balancing for systematic selection with equal probabilities, tested on county population totals with Cochran's variance estimator. Better balance reduced bias but not necessarily estimated variance. No cluster case.

authors: D. Litwok; A. Nichols; A. Shivji; R. B. Olsen
title: Selecting Districts and Schools for Impact Studies in Education: A Simulation Study of Different Strategies
venue_or_arxiv: Report, published 2023-01-06 (venue not shown on page)
what_it_holds: Simulation comparing recruitment order, random selection weighted by district size, and balanced selection favouring typical districts and schools. Random selection of districts gave the most consistently strong generalizability; balanced selection did about as well at the school level. Compares sample average to population average; does not address interval coverage with few clusters.

title: Stratified Sampling Using Cluster Analysis: A Sample Selection Strategy for Improved Generalizations From Experiments
what_it_holds: Model-based balanced-sampling framework for selecting sites for experiments: cluster analysis forms strata, then units are chosen by distance rankings. Reanalysis of a completed experiment shows better covariate balance and fewer coverage errors than the actual sample. A purposive, distance-based selection of a few sites with model-based justification.

title: Using Survey Data to Obtain More Representative Site Samples for Impact Studies
what_it_holds: Uses survey data to set limits on how many sites of each type a study sample can include. Site-level selection; abstract does not discuss variance estimation.

authors: J. Siddique; Z. Li; M. J. O'Brien
title: Covariate-constrained randomization in cluster randomized 2 x 2 factorial trials: application to a diabetes prevention study
what_it_holds: Constrained randomization chooses among covariate-balanced allocations of clusters. With 8 to 12 clusters, unadjusted analysis after constrained randomization is conservative in coverage and type 1 error, and adjusting for covariates costs degrees of freedom. Suggests randomization-based inference as future work. A trial analogue of rejective selection of few clusters.

title: A Comparison of Methods of Inference in Randomized Experiments from a Restricted Set of Allocations
what_it_holds: Compares inference methods after Mahalanobis rerandomization, against the Li et al. (2018) asymptotic approach, in a large Monte Carlo study. Some alternatives beat the asymptotic method at small or moderate sample sizes.

title: Penalized balanced sampling
what_it_holds: Cube-algorithm implementation that selects penalized balanced samples using linear mixed models at the design stage. Horvitz-Thompson estimators from such samples are highly efficient when the mixed model fits.

title: With-Replacement Balanced Sampling
what_it_holds: Three with-replacement balanced sampling algorithms from a generalization of the cube method, with a variance approximation. Not cluster-specific.

authors: R. Jauslin; E. Eustache; Y. Tille
title: Enhanced Cube Implementation For Highly Stratified Population
what_it_holds: Faster cube selection for populations with many strata. Implementation paper.

authors: B. Panahbehagh; M. Mohebbi; A. M. HosseiniNasab
title: Intelligent n-Means Spatial Sampling
what_it_holds: Spatially spread survey samples using clustering on inclusion probabilities and graphical sampling. Evaluated on dispersion metrics; abstract does not address design-based inference or variance estimation.

title: Two-Stage Sampling from a Prediction Point of View
what_it_holds: Prediction intervals for a population total under two-stage cluster sampling with a variance-component model. Intervals differ noticeably when few clusters are sampled. Simulation reports model-based and design-based coverage, close to nominal for large samples and below nominal for moderate and small ones.

authors: Z. An; M. Dagdoug; D. Haziza; Y. Tille
title: Agnostic Model-Assisted Estimation with Machine Learning for Survey Data
what_it_holds: Model-assisted survey estimation with any machine learning learner via cross-fitting. Design-unbiased, with cross-fitted variance estimators and confidence intervals. Does not mention clusters, and is not about choosing which units to label.

authors: B. Wang; F. Li; M. Yu
title: Conformal causal inference for cluster randomized trials: model-robust inference without asymptotic approximations
what_it_holds: Finite-sample conformal intervals for cluster-level and individual-level counterfactual differences in cluster randomized trials, without many-cluster asymptotics. Cluster-level prediction with few clusters, but not the K calibration clusters plus o labelled target units setting.

title: Design-based conformal prediction
what_it_holds: Conformal prediction sets with finite-sample coverage under design-based inference for a finite population from complex survey designs. Abstract does not name the designs or say whether cluster sampling is covered [verify].

authors: C. Lee; S. Jung; H. G. Hong
title: Predicting Current Outcomes From Historical Survey Data With Weighted Conformal Prediction
what_it_holds: Weighted conformal prediction for survey data under covariate shift between survey years, accounting for the sampling design. Not clustered.

title: Selection from Hierarchical Data with Conformal e-values
what_it_holds: Conformal e-values for selection with FDR control when data are grouped, with subsampling and hierarchical variants. Selection, not prediction sets for a new group.

title: CAOS: Conformal Aggregation of One-Shot Predictors
what_it_holds: Conformal sets for one-shot prediction on a new task from a single labelled example, aggregating predictors with leave-one-out calibration, with a marginal coverage proof despite broken exchangeability. Baselines named are split conformal methods; no comparison with hierarchical conformal shown in the abstract.

authors: Y. Liu; A. W. Levis; S.-L. Normand; L. Han
title: Multi-Source Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
what_it_holds: Prediction intervals for a target population from several source sites under distribution shift, with efficient influence functions and an application to hospital length of stay. No labelled target units in the abstract.

authors: A. Fisch; J. Maynez; R. A. Hofer; B. Dhingra; A. Globerson; W. W. Cohen
title: Stratified Prediction-Powered Inference for Hybrid Language Model Evaluation
what_it_holds: StratPPI: stratified PPI with confidence intervals based on stratified sampling theory, valid without assumptions on the automated labeller. Stratification and allocation of labels narrow the intervals. Unit-level strata, not cluster selection.

title: Adaptive Stratified Active Statistical Inference
what_it_holds: AdaStrat-ASI replaces the single global sampling rule of active statistical inference with stratum-specific policies guided by a label-free scouting phase, with lower asymptotic variance than ASI. Strata are regions of input space, not clusters of correlated units.

title: Active Multiple-Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: Active PPI with several predictors of different cost, routing instances to predictors and to gold-standard labelling. Instance-level; no clusters.

authors: A. S. Wadekar; J. P. Reiter
title: Evaluating Binary Outcome Classifiers Estimated from Survey Data
what_it_holds: Survey-weighted estimates of classifier metrics as finite-population quantities, using weights from complex sampling designs.

authors: T. Hong; D. Lim; W. Bae
title: Beyond Point Estimates: Reliable Evaluation of Prediction Performance Metrics under Clustered Data
what_it_holds: Cluster-robust sandwich confidence intervals for classifier metrics under clustered data. No conformal sets.

authors: L. Alvarez; B. Ferman; K. Wuthrich
title: Inference with few treated units
what_it_holds: Survey of inference methods when there are one or a few treated units or clusters, where large-sample approximations are unreliable. Econometric framing, not sampling design.

title: Benchmarking Active Spot Selection for Cost-Efficient Spatial Transcriptomics
what_it_holds: Benchmarks uncertainty-based and diversity-based (CoreSet, TypiClust-style) active spot selection against uniform random sampling on two cohorts, 160 configurations, budgets 5 to 50 percent, with patient-level cross-validation. Active strategies did not consistently beat random at small budgets. Reports point estimates only, no intervals or guarantees. Spot-level, not cluster-level.

title: SCR2-ST: Combine Single Cell with Spatial Transcriptomics for Efficient Active Sampling via Reinforcement Learning
what_it_holds: Active sampling for spatial transcriptomics by reinforcement learning. Only the title was seen in search results; abstract not read [verify].

title: Measuring What Histology Can Predict: Leakage-Stratified Evaluation for Spatial Transcriptomics
what_it_holds: 360 Visium slides over 12 organs. Reported per-gene correlation changes by about an order of magnitude with holdout strategy (random spot, patient, whole study) and with pooling. Patient-level splits add little because most slides come from one donor. Bears on how cluster structure in HEST-type data affects honest evaluation.

title: Patient-Held-Out Evaluation of Pathology Foundation Models for Histology-to-Expression Prediction
what_it_holds: 119 sections from 62 patients over four organs, leave-one-patient-out comparison of five encoders and gene-selection rules. No coverage guarantees.

title: CHRep: Cross-modal Histology Representation and Post-hoc Calibration for Spatial Gene Expression Prediction
what_it_holds: Histology-to-expression model with a post-hoc calibration module for cross-slide shift. Calibration means bias correction, not conformal coverage.

authors: M. A. Hidiroglou; J. N. K. Rao
title: Variance Estimation in Two-Phase Sampling
what_it_holds: Notes that the Horvitz-Thompson variance estimator can be unstable or negative under unequal probabilities and extends Sen-Yates-Grundy to two-phase designs.
